observation: At original Kernel readiness, a guarded change of byte0x800594f8 from observed01 to00 followed by the original Down/Cross Battle-menu input reaches visible original battle presentation on both discs. Disc1 reaches frame4065 and Disc2 frame4064. A matched Disc1 control preserving01, with identical timing and controller input, remains flat teal at4065. Three additional Disc1 Cross inputs visibly alter command/attack-point and actor/target presentation. Twelve entry/conditional/table-copy instruction windows across four captures match independently decoded original sources. Two Disc1 coldboots have byte-identical full RAM at4065 before additional inputs.
interpretation: The original mode2 byte is a useful battle-entry research control. Original instructions at0x80071050 read it, with zero branching to0x800710f0; the nonzero path loads directory(16,2) file1 at0x801e0000 and conditionally calls0x801e0a34. This supports further battle-adapter recovery. It does not yet establish a complete retail state setup, a typed formation selector, battle readiness, combat rules or return semantics. The byte has other original consumers, so the debug-gate label identifies the studied conditional rather than its complete meaning.

limitations: Only Kernel readiness is asserted; no battle readiness predicate or typed battle adapter is established.
All four programs are explicit analysis probes; the gate write is not a recovered retail progression setup.
No native battle, battle formulas, formation schema, victory/reward/return-to-field behavior or hardware timing is established.
The observed original byte1 at Kernel readiness is not claimed to be its static executable initializer; other original stores/consumers require review.
The matched entry control supports the observed byte-level setup difference, not the claim that every effect of that byte is confined to the debug overlay.
Visible input response is not a recovered damage formula, target-state hash, victory/reward result or field-return validation.
The original-source decoder remains a private evidence probe, not a reviewed general importer.
This finding is a Phase1 research seed and does not retroactively alter the preserved Phase0 verification snapshot.
